title: Nvidia employee detained in Taiwan as part of chip smuggling probe — held on suspicion of falsifying business documents, company says smuggling 'a nonstarter'
content: Taiwan's prosecutors say they've detained a man surnamed Chang on suspicion of falsifying business documents, after investigators searched his home and workplace.

title: Re-examining the DDR4 gaming gap with Intel’s LGA 1700 CPUs in mid-2026 — performance drops of 14% on average, and up to 25% in some games
content: Given the unprecedented surge in memory prices, we’re looking back on Intel’s LGA 1700 stack of CPUs to see how DDR4 and DDR5 match up with our modern gaming suite in 2026.

title: Magnitude 7.1 quake strikes Japan's Kumamoto; TSMC activates emergency protocols at local fab
content: A powerful earthquake struck Japan's Kyushu region at 4:27 p.m. on July 28. The Japan Meteorological Agency initially estimated the quake at magnitude 7.1 with a depth of 6.2 miles (10 kilometers). The strongest shaking was recorded in Uki City and Hikawa Town in Kumamoto Prefecture, reaching seismic intensity 7 on Japan's scale. TSMC's Japan fab in Kikuyo Town experienced an intensity of 5+, and a tsunami warning was issued.

title: Squeezed by China, Taiwan ODMs pivot to AI for new growth
content: China's notebook manufacturing industry is rising rapidly just as Taiwan's ODMs retreat from notebook assembly, but Wistron chairman Simon Lin said the shift also reflects new opportunities as companies pivot toward AI. Lin said each era has its own mission, and many companies would rather move notebook resources into other areas.

title: TCC launches Europe listing plan as revenue from the region reaches 44%
content: Taiwan Cement Corp. (TCC) formally launched its Europe listing plan, Project Arcadia, on July 27 after holding a video meeting with its first group of international investment banks and advisers. The company said the move marked a major step in its effort to build a capital markets presence in Europe.

title: Nvidia invests in Ilya Sutskever's SSI, providing access to Vera Rubin compute platform
content: Nvidia has made a strategic investment in Safe Superintelligence Inc. and announced a long-term partnership with the secretive AI lab founded by OpenAI co-founder Ilya Sutskever, giving SSI access to Nvidia's next-generation Vera Rubin systems and expanding its computing capacity by an order of magnitude.

title: Qualcomm chip price hike to squeeze China's Android makers on two fronts
content: China's smartphone brands are bracing for a new round of cost pressure after Qualcomm reportedly notified customers of double-digit percentage price increases on products shipped from September 1—a move that compounds already rising memory and materials costs hitting the Android supply chain.

title: Samsung trims Z Fold8 display module 10% using Flex Titanium
content: Samsung Electronics has introduced Flex Titanium technology in its next-generation foldables, the Galaxy Z Fold8 and Z Fold8 Ultra, cutting display module thickness by 10% to make room for a larger battery and improve user experience. According to ZDNet Korea, Samsung is applying the technology to these two models for the first time.

title: Display industry earnings season shifts spotlight from panel prices to transformation strategies
content: Taiwan's display supply chain enters second-quarter earnings season this week, with Coretronic reporting results on July 28, followed by AUO and Radiant Opto-Electronics (ROEC) on July 30 and BenQ Materials (BMC) on July 31.

title: Automotive chip demand surges in 2Q26 on EV reset
content: Automotive chip demand surprised to the upside in the second quarter of 2026, with industry players saying the market could stay hot in the second half as new EV architectures become clearer and customers rebuild inventories. The strongest signal came from Texas Instruments (TI), which said the strength in automotive chips was completely unexpected.

title: Google TPU surge and Meta capacity push fuel CSP capex wave
content: AI demand and whether the boom is heading into a bubble are back in focus, and capital expenditure by cloud service providers (CSPs) and their supply chains is emerging as a key gauge. Google has already said it will raise capex again in 2027, and industry watchers expect AWS and Microsoft to follow, keeping AI infrastructure momentum strong with more capital injections.

title: UMT posts record revenue in 1H26 on growing LEO satellite demand
content: Universal Microwave Technology (UMT), a manufacturer of satellite and millimeter-wave (mmWave) communications components, benefited from continued growth in demand for low Earth orbit (LEO) satellite communications products in the first half of 2026.

title: CXMT's record IPO and Apple talks collide with US curbs as DRAM tightens
content: AI-driven demand is tightening the global memory market just as China's leading DRAM producer, ChangXin Memory Technologies, or CXMT, accelerates capacity expansion after a record IPO.

title: SK Hynix enters LPDDR6 production race with Xiaomi first in line
content: SK Hynix reportedly plans to begin mass production and shipments of LPDDR6 in the second half of 2026, with Xiaomi expected to become its first customer for mobile devices. Industry sources said an early LPDDR6 launch would strengthen SK Hynix's position in premium mobile DRAM and lay the groundwork for expansion into AI server memory.

title: AI memory demand lifts WF6 prices as PERIC Special Gases adopts market-based pricing
content: Surging demand for AI servers and advanced memory devices is tightening the global supply of tungsten hexafluoride (WF6), drawing increased attention to one of the semiconductor industry's most important specialty gases.

title: Samsung eyes Chinese DRAM sourcing to cut costs, expand budget-phone share in China
content: Samsung Electronics is evaluating the use of lower-cost Chinese DRAM in some smartphones as it seeks to offset rising component costs and regain momentum in China's highly competitive budget handset market.
